passage: Trisha had spent two evenings reading the ward's water reports for her science project, and the numbers about the river made her want to do something. Deepika, from the next lane, told her about a peaceful cleanup walk on Sunday, with permission from the ward office. But there was a maths test on Monday and only two hours to spare. Trisha checked the notice, saw the organisers had marshals and drinking water, and showed it to Papa. "I'll be by the river bridge with Deepika, from ten till noon. I'll share my location." Papa read the notice twice. "Home by twelve-thirty." Trisha nodded, pulled on her old shoes, and put the revision notes in her bag.

qa.q: Who told Trisha about the cleanup walk?
What was Trisha feeling about the cause, and what showed it?
qa.a: Trisha felt moved and eager to act; two evenings of reading the water reports and the wish to do something show it.

qa.q: Which steps made Trisha's plan safe?
qa.a: Checking the notice for permission, marshals and water, telling Papa where and when, and sharing the location. 🙂

qa.q: How might Papa feel about being told the plan?
qa.a: Probably reassured and trusting, since Papa read the notice twice and agreed to a return time.

grounding: Trisha feels the pull of an environmental cause, learns the facts, picks a peaceful permitted walk and tells Papa where she will be.

passage:
At the school eco-club meeting, Shreya could barely sit still. The lake behind the colony had turned green and smelly, and she'd seen dead fish at the edge that morning. "We should march to the municipal office tomorrow!"

Ishita, the club secretary, said, "Do we know why it's green?"

Shreya didn't. So on Wednesday, with Mrs Rao, the biology teacher, they collected water samples and looked them up. Sewage from a broken drain, the internet and a local paper said. On Thursday, they went to the municipal ward office together and asked, politely, who was responsible. A clerk showed them the complaint form.

Shreya still wanted to do something bigger. They planned a Sunday clean-up of the lake edge with permission from the residents' association, and a petition with facts and photos.

On Saturday night, Shreya left a note on the fridge for her parents: "Lake clean-up, 7 to 10 a.m., with eco-club and Mrs Rao. Phone on." Then she set her alarm.

qa.q: What did the water turn out to be polluted by?
qa.a: The lake was polluted by sewage from a broken drain.

qa.q: What was Shreya feeling at the start of the eco-club meeting?
qa.a: Shreya felt upset and restless, eager to act quickly after seeing the dead fish.

qa.q: Which steps made Shreya's action wise?
qa.a: Shreya learned the facts with Mrs Rao, went through the ward office, chose a permitted clean-up and petition, and told her parents where she would be.

qa.q: How might Ishita see Shreya's energy?
qa.a: Ishita seems to value it but wants it guided by facts, which is why she asked why the lake was green.

grounding: It shows a teen pulled to act on an environmental cause, learning the facts, choosing peaceful and lawful ways and telling a trusted adult where she will be.

passage:
Dear Amma and Appa,

I'm writing this so you can read it properly before we talk.

You know about the paper leak in the state board exam. Thousands of us studied for months, and now some people bought the questions. I'm so angry I can't sleep. Imran and some seniors are organising a silent march on Saturday from the school gate to the education office to ask for a fair re-exam.

Before saying yes, I checked. The march has written police permission; Imran showed me the letter. It's from ten to twelve, on the main road, no shouting, just placards. Two teachers are coming. I've read the news reports and the board's statement, so I know what we're actually asking for.

I want to go. I'll walk with the teachers, keep my phone charged, and send you my location every half hour. If anything feels unsafe, I'll leave and call you.

Can we talk tonight after dinner?

Dolma

qa.q: What time does the silent march run?
qa.a: The march runs from ten to twelve.

qa.q: What was Dolma feeling about the paper leak?
qa.a: Dolma felt so angry about the unfairness that sleep was hard.

qa.q: What did Dolma do that made the plan safer and wiser?
qa.a: Dolma checked the permission letter, read the news and the board's statement, planned to walk with teachers and share a location every half hour.

qa.q: How might Amma and Appa feel reading this letter?
qa.a: They might feel worried about the march, but also reassured and proud that Dolma checked the facts and made a safety plan.

grounding: It shows a teen pulled to act on exam fairness who learns the facts, chooses a peaceful, lawful march and tells trusted adults where they will be.
